passages.text: Woe to you, O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed. When you have finished betraying, you will be betrayed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the destroyer.
You destroy others.
No one has destroyed you.
You betray others.
No one has betrayed you.
When you finish destroying, others will destroy you.
When you finish betraying, others will betray you.
passages.original: ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד וְאַתָּה֙ לֹ֣א שָׁד֔וּד וּבוֹגֵ֖ד וְלֹא־ בָ֣גְדוּ ב֑וֹ כַּהֲתִֽמְךָ֤ שׁוֹדֵד֙ תּוּשַּׁ֔ד כַּנְּלֹתְךָ֥ לִבְגֹּ֖ד יִבְגְּדוּ־ בָֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
We ask the LORD to show us grace.
We wait for the LORD.
We trust the LORD.
We ask the LORD to give us strength every morning.
We ask the LORD to save us when we are in trouble.
passages.original: יְהוָ֥ה חָנֵּ֖נוּ לְךָ֣ קִוִּ֑ינוּ הֱיֵ֤ה זְרֹעָם֙ לַבְּקָרִ֔ים אַף־ יְשׁוּעָתֵ֖נוּ בְּעֵ֥ת צָרָֽה׃

passages.text: The peoples flee the thunder of Your voice; the nations scatter when You rise.
passages.sermon:
God speaks with a mighty voice.
Many peoples hear this loud sound.
The peoples run away from the sound of God's voice.
God rises up in power.
When God rises, the nations scatter.
The nations break apart and flee because of God's greatness.
passages.original: מִקּ֣וֹל הָמ֔וֹן נָדְד֖וּ עַמִּ֑ים מֵר֣וֹמְמֻתֶ֔ךָ נָפְצ֖וּ גּוֹיִֽם׃

passages.text: Your spoil, O nations, is gathered as by locusts; like a swarm of locusts men sweep over it.
passages.sermon:
God judges the nations.
He takes away what they have gained.
People gather the spoil from the nations.
They gather it quickly, like locusts gather food.
Many people rush in, like a swarm of locusts.
They sweep over the spoil and take it away.
passages.original: וְאֻסַּ֣ף שְׁלַלְכֶ֔ם אֹ֖סֶף הֶֽחָסִ֑יל כְּמַשַּׁ֥ק גֵּבִ֖ים שׁוֹקֵ֥ק בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is exalted.
The LORD lives in a high place.
The LORD has filled Zion with justice.
The LORD has filled Zion with righteousness.
passages.original: נִשְׂגָּ֣ב יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י שֹׁכֵ֖ן מָר֑וֹם מִלֵּ֣א צִיּ֔וֹן מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

passages.text: He will be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is exalted.
He lives on high.
He fills Zion with justice and righteousness.
He is a sure foundation for your times.
He gives you a storehouse of salvation.
He gives you wisdom.
He gives you knowledge.
The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֙ אֱמוּנַ֣ת עִתֶּ֔יךָ חֹ֥סֶן יְשׁוּעֹ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת וָדָ֑עַת יִרְאַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה הִ֥יא אוֹצָרֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Behold, their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
passages.sermon:
The valiant ones belong to the people of the city.
These valiant ones cry out loudly in the streets.
The envoys of peace are present among them.
The envoys of peace weep with great bitterness.
passages.original: הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם צָעֲק֖וּ חֻ֑צָה מַלְאֲכֵ֣י שָׁל֔וֹם מַ֖ר יִבְכָּיֽוּן׃

passages.text: The highways are deserted; travel has ceased. The treaty has been broken, the witnesses are despised, and human life is disregarded.
passages.sermon:
The highways are empty.
No one travels on the roads.
People have broken the treaty.
They despise the cities.
They do not value human life.
passages.original: נָשַׁ֣מּוּ מְסִלּ֔וֹת שָׁבַ֖ת עֹבֵ֣ר אֹ֑רַח הֵפֵ֤ר בְּרִית֙ מָאַ֣ס עָרִ֔ים לֹ֥א חָשַׁ֖ב אֱנֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and decayed. Sharon is like a desert; Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
passages.sermon:
The land mourns.
The land languishes.
Lebanon feels shame.
Lebanon has decayed.
Sharon has become like a desert.
Bashan shakes off its leaves.
Carmel shakes off its leaves.
passages.original: אָבַ֤ל אֻמְלְלָה֙ אָ֔רֶץ הֶחְפִּ֥יר לְבָנ֖וֹן קָמַ֑ל הָיָ֤ה הַשָּׁרוֹן֙ כָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה וְנֹעֵ֥ר בָּשָׁ֖ן וְכַרְמֶֽל׃

passages.text: “Now I will arise,” says the LORD. “Now I will lift Myself up. Now I will be exalted.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is powerful and holy.
The LORD says, “Now I will arise.”
The LORD says, “Now I will lift Myself up.”
The LORD says, “Now I will be exalted.”
passages.original: עַתָּ֥ה אָק֖וּם יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה עַתָּה֙ אֵֽרוֹמָ֔ם עַתָּ֖ה אֶנָּשֵֽׂא׃

passages.text: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that will consume you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
You produce only worthless things.
You conceive chaff.
You give birth to stubble.
Your words and actions are empty.
Your own breath becomes a fire.
This fire will consume you.
passages.original: תַּהֲר֥וּ חֲשַׁ֖שׁ תֵּ֣לְדוּ קַ֑שׁ רוּחֲכֶ֕ם אֵ֖שׁ תֹּאכַלְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: The peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking.
God is powerful and just.
God will judge the peoples.
The peoples will burn up.
They will become ashes.
They will be like thorns.
Someone cuts down thorns.
Someone sets thorns on fire.
The thorns burn quickly.
The peoples will burn in the same way.
passages.original: וְהָי֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים מִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת שִׂ֑יד קוֹצִ֥ים כְּסוּחִ֖ים בָּאֵ֥שׁ יִצַּֽתּוּ׃ס

passages.text: You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My might.”
passages.sermon: God speaks to all people.\r\nPeople who are far away, listen to what God has done.\r\nPeople who are near, recognize God's power.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי וּדְע֥וּ קְרוֹבִ֖ים גְּבֻרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the ungodly: “Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?”
passages.sermon:
The sinners live in Zion.
The sinners feel afraid.
The ungodly people tremble.
They ask a question.
They say, “Who among us can live with a consuming fire?”
They say, “Who among us can live with everlasting flames?”
passages.original: פָּחֲד֤וּ בְצִיּוֹן֙ חַטָּאִ֔ים אָחֲזָ֥ה רְעָדָ֖ה חֲנֵפִ֑ים מִ֣י׀ יָג֣וּר לָ֗נוּ אֵ֚שׁ אוֹכֵלָ֔ה מִי־ יָג֥וּר לָ֖נוּ מוֹקְדֵ֥י עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: He who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity, who refuses gain from extortion, whose hand never takes a bribe, who stops his ears against murderous plots and shuts his eyes tightly against evil— he will dwell on the heights; the mountain fortress will be his refuge; his food will be provided and his water assured.
passages.sermon:
A righteous person walks in justice.
He speaks honestly.
He refuses to profit from oppression.
He never takes a bribe.
He keeps his hands clean from corruption.
He blocks his ears from hearing about murder.
He shuts his eyes so he does not see evil.
This person will live in a high place.
A mountain fortress will be his safe home.
He will always have food.
He will always have water.
passages.original: הֹלֵ֣ךְ צְדָק֔וֹת וְדֹבֵ֖ר מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים מֹאֵ֞ס בְּבֶ֣צַע מַעֲשַׁקּ֗וֹת נֹעֵ֤ר כַּפָּיו֙ מִתְּמֹ֣ךְ בַּשֹּׁ֔חַד אֹטֵ֤ם אָזְנוֹ֙ מִשְּׁמֹ֣עַ דָּמִ֔ים וְעֹצֵ֥ם עֵינָ֖יו מֵרְא֥וֹת בְּרָֽע׃ ה֚וּא מְרוֹמִ֣ים יִשְׁכֹּ֔ן מְצָד֥וֹת סְלָעִ֖ים מִשְׂגַּבּ֑וֹ לַחְמ֣וֹ נִתָּ֔ן מֵימָ֖יו נֶאֱמָנִֽים׃

passages.text: Your eyes will see the King in His beauty and behold a land that stretches afar.
passages.sermon:
You will see the King.
The King is beautiful.
Your eyes will look at Him.
You will see a land.
The land is wide and far.
You will look at this land.
passages.original: מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּיָפְי֖וֹ תֶּחֱזֶ֣ינָה עֵינֶ֑יךָ תִּרְאֶ֖ינָה אֶ֥רֶץ מַרְחַקִּֽים׃

passages.text: Your mind will ponder the former terror: “Where is he who tallies? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?”
passages.sermon:
You will remember a time of fear.
You will think about the terror you once felt.
You will ask, “Where is the one who counted?”
You will ask, “Where is the one who weighed?”
You will ask, “Where is the one who counted the towers?”
passages.original: לִבְּךָ֖ יֶהְגֶּ֣ה אֵימָ֑ה אַיֵּ֤ה סֹפֵר֙ אַיֵּ֣ה שֹׁקֵ֔ל אַיֵּ֖ה סֹפֵ֥ר אֶת־ הַמִּגְדָּלִֽים׃

passages.text: You will no longer see the insolent, a people whose speech is unintelligible, who stammer in a language you cannot understand.
passages.sermon:
You will not see the insolent people.
They are a people with harsh and strange speech.
You cannot understand their language.
They stammer in words that have no meaning for you.
passages.original: אֶת־ עַ֥ם נוֹעָ֖ז לֹ֣א תִרְאֶ֑ה עַ֣ם עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ מִשְּׁמ֔וֹעַ נִלְעַ֥ג לָשׁ֖וֹן אֵ֥ין בִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful pasture, a tent that does not wander; its tent pegs will not be pulled up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
passages.sermon:
Zion is the city where God’s people gather for appointed feasts.
Look at Zion.
Your eyes will see Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is a place of peace and safety.
Jerusalem is like a tent that does not move.
No one will pull up its tent pegs.
No one will break any of its cords.
passages.original: חֲזֵ֣ה צִיּ֔וֹן קִרְיַ֖ת מֽוֹעֲדֵ֑נוּ עֵינֶיךָ֩ תִרְאֶ֨ינָה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם נָוֶ֣ה שַׁאֲנָ֗ן אֹ֤הֶל בַּל־ יִצְעָן֙ בַּל־ יִסַּ֤ע יְתֵֽדֹתָיו֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְכָל־ חֲבָלָ֖יו בַּל־ יִנָּתֵֽקוּ׃

passages.text: But there the Majestic One, our LORD, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals, where no galley with oars will row, and no majestic vessel will pass.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our Majestic One.
He will be with us in Zion.
He will provide a place for us.
This place will have rivers.
These rivers will be wide.
There will be broad canals.
No galley with oars will travel there.
No majestic ship will pass through it.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ שָׁ֞ם אַדִּ֤יר יְהוָה֙ לָ֔נוּ מְקוֹם־ נְהָרִ֥ים יְאֹרִ֖ים רַחֲבֵ֣י יָדָ֑יִם בַּל־ תֵּ֤לֶךְ בּוֹ֙ אֳנִי־ שַׁ֔יִט וְצִ֥י אַדִּ֖יר לֹ֥א יַעַבְרֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King. It is He who will save us.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our Judge.
The LORD decides what is right and wrong for us.
The LORD is our lawgiver.
The LORD gives us His laws.
The LORD is our King.
The LORD rules over us.
The LORD will save us.
He alone rescues us.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֔נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מְחֹקְקֵ֑נוּ יְהוָ֥ה מַלְכֵּ֖נוּ ה֥וּא יוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail. Then an abundance of spoils will be divided, and even the lame will carry off plunder.
passages.sermon:
Your ropes are loose.
Your ropes do not hold tight.
You cannot make the mast stand firm.
You cannot spread the sail.
Then people will divide much plunder.
Even those who are lame will take the spoil.
passages.original: נִטְּשׁ֖וּ חֲבָלָ֑יִךְ בַּל־ יְחַזְּק֤וּ כֵן־ תָּרְנָם֙ בַּל־ פָּ֣רְשׂוּ נֵ֔ס אָ֣ז חֻלַּ֤ק עַֽד־ שָׁלָל֙ מַרְבֶּ֔ה פִּסְחִ֖ים בָּ֥זְזוּ בַֽז׃

passages.text: And no resident of Zion will say, “I am sick.” The people who dwell there will be forgiven of iniquity.
passages.sermon: Zion is the city where God’s people live.\r\nNo one who lives in Zion will say, “I am sick.”\r\nGod will forgive the sins of the people who live there.
passages.original: וּבַל־ יֹאמַ֥ר שָׁכֵ֖ן חָלִ֑יתִי הָעָ֛ם הַיֹּשֵׁ֥ב בָּ֖הּ נְשֻׂ֥א עָוֺֽן׃
